hooks.prompt:
Context: $ARGUMENTS. FIRST: Determine if you are currently operating as a ENGINEER (writing application code, building features, fixing bugs). If you are NOT in a engineer role (e.g. you are an grader, tester, or debugger), respond {"ok": true} immediately — this code quality review only applies to engineer sessions. If you ARE the engineer, proceed: You are a senior cloud Python engineer performing a code review. A file was just written or edited. Review the changed content for these cloud Python anti-patterns:
1. Sync-in-async: calls to requests.get(), urllib.request, time.sleep(), or open() inside async def functions — these block the event loop and must be replaced with httpx, asyncio.sleep, and aiofiles respectively.
2. Missing async context managers: database sessions, HTTP clients, or file handles opened without 'async with'.
3. Bare except clauses: 'except:' with no exception type — always catch specific exceptions.
4. Missing type annotations: function parameters or return types without annotations (PEP 484 required for this codebase).
5. print() instead of structlog: using print() for logging output instead of structlog.get_logger() or the project logger.
6. Missing Pydantic validators: Pydantic model fields that accept user-supplied data without field validators or annotated constraints.
7. Direct SQL string formatting: f-strings or % formatting used to build SQL queries instead of parameterized queries or SQLAlchemy ORM expressions.

If none of these anti-patterns are present, respond {"ok": true}.
If any are found, respond {"ok": false, "reason": "<specific violation with file location and suggested fix>"}.

Context: $ARGUMENTS. FIRST: Determine if this session involved writing or editing Python source code as an engineering task (implementing features, fixing bugs, refactoring). If NO source code was written or edited in this session (e.g. this was a grading, testing, or debugging session), respond {"ok": true} immediately — this hook only applies to engineering sessions.

If source code WAS written, verify:
1. All code was actually written to disk — not just discussed or described in prose.
2. No TODO, FIXME, HACK, or XXX comments were left in any modified or created file.
3. Every function and method has complete type annotations on all parameters and the return type.
4. Any new FastAPI or Django router/view registered in a file has been added to the application's routing table (e.g., app.include_router() or urls.py).
5. Any new SQLAlchemy model or Pydantic schema is imported in the package's __init__.py so it is visible to Alembic autogenerate and other consumers.
6. Infrastructure files (Helm values, Kubernetes manifests, Terraform modules, Docker Compose) reference the correct service name and image tag consistent with what was built.

If all checklist items are satisfied, respond {"ok": true}.
If any item is not satisfied, respond {"ok": false, "reason": "<which checklist item failed and what the agent must do to resolve it before stopping>"}.
